label: Brousse du Rove
note: Made from whole milk, not from whey like other brousses; farm production only

about.text: Brousse du Rove is a fresh goat cheese from Le Rove near Marseille, made only on the farm from whole milk of the Rove goat breed. It has had a protected designation of origin since 2018 and is traditionally eaten sweetened with orange-flower water.

sources.text: The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.text: Milk is scalded, cooled a little and acidified with vinegar, the same heat-and-acid set as chhena.

sources.text: The table, the facts and the words on how it is made, from these.

steps.name: mould
steps.note: The curds are skimmed off and filled into conical moulds about 12 cm long.

sources.text: The table, the facts and the words on how it is made, from these.
Whole milk of Rove goats heated to about 89 C and flocculated with white vinegar, not rennet and not whey-based; unripened, sold within 8 days

facts.v: earlier brousses were re-cooked whey (recuite); this one is milk, since at least the 19th century
